MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
4 marks: Analyses effectively how the text explores the paradox of boredom
3 marks: Analyses how the text explores the paradox of boredom
2 marks: Explains how the text explores the paradox of boredom
1 marks: Describes a relevant point about the extract

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
The feature article explores the ways in which boredom is both feared and essential to the creative human spirit through the use of irony and juxtaposition. Ryan, through his use of critical experts such as Mary Mann who sets up the notion that ‘boredom is a challenge’, expresses the idea that we must aspire to boredom when, ironically, it is a basic human trait. The interweaving of the anecdote of Christopher Knight’s ‘full-Robinson Crusoe’ disappearance creates a personal inflection that is both familiar and alien to the reader; we can empathise with his regret at the loss of ‘somewhere between quiet and solitude . . . stillness’, but baulk at the idea of ‘simply [being] alone in the forest, a solitary adventurer discovering what mysteries lay [beyond] boredom’. The paradox that ‘being challenged is often good for us’, creates the image of the necessity of boredom, itself a paradox.
